standard.title: Evaluate success and sustainability
standard.description: evaluate the success of design ideas and solutions based on personal preferences and including sustainability
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can evaluate what they made using personal preferences (AC9TDEFP01). They have shared opinions about their design. They have not yet evaluated against sustainability considerations, reflected on environmental impacts, or compared design ideas for strengths and weaknesses in a structured way.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students evaluate the success of design ideas and solutions based on personal preferences and sustainability considerations.

nodes.label: Evaluating against personal preferences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on and record a judgement about a design idea or solution based on personal preferences, identifying strengths and areas for improvement
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least one strength and one weakness of a design or solution using personal preferences as the basis
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on design ideas and solutions across the full design process — describe what meets the design need and what could be improved; record judgements using audio, video or written/drawn responses; share with others
wider: Describe how design ideas meet the needs of those who will use the solution — use audio or video recording to capture the evaluation; review the recording and identify changes
Share design strengths and weaknesses with the class — explain how playground equipment might be unsuitable for some children and suggest specific improvements

response_modes.reason: Evaluation requires students to apply a criterion to their work — but at Y1-2, the criterion of personal preference is itself vague without scaffolding. A structure (what did you want it to do? does it do that? what would you change and why?) moves evaluation from 'I like it/I don't like it' to reasoned judgement about design success.

success_criteria: Names at least one strength of the design or solution
Names at least one area for improvement — not just 'make it better' but a specific change
nodes.hinge_reason: Evaluative reasoning against personal preferences is the prerequisite for Node 2's sustainability evaluation — Node 2 extends the same reasoning structure to environmental criteria. Students who cannot evaluate against any criterion cannot take on a second, less familiar one.

nodes.label: Evaluating sustainability impacts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on the environmental impacts of a solution and consider alternative approaches that minimise negative impacts
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one environmental impact of making a solution and suggest one way that impact could be reduced
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on environmental impacts across multiple production contexts (food packaging, material waste, water use); identify negative impacts and suggest alternative approaches; connect sustainability evaluation to both design ideas and making processes
wider: Identify the negative environmental impacts of different food packaging options — suggest how packaging could be redesigned to minimise impact; explain the trade-offs
Reflect on the challenges of producing a solution (growing food, making a structure, preparing a snack) and record what would be done differently to reduce environmental impact next time

response_modes.reason: Sustainability impacts are not immediately visible at Y1-2 level — students need to encounter them in multiple, concrete production contexts before the evaluative habit generalises. Food packaging, water use and material waste are distinct enough to reveal different aspects of environmental impact, each making the abstract concept tangible.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The food packaging redesign direction requires students to apply sustainability evaluation as a design constraint — not just notice impact but propose a better design. This is richer than minimum evaluation and builds genuine design thinking with sustainability as a criterion.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one environmental impact of a production activity
Suggests at least one concrete alternative that would reduce that impact
